Guidance

National Fraud Initiative: public-sector data specifications

This guide sets out the dataset specifications for the National Fraud Initiative (NFI) 2026 to 2027 national exercise and NFI council tax single person discount 2026 to 2027 and 2027 to 2028 exercises.

From:
Cabinet Office and Public Sector Fraud Authority
Published:
20 March 2015
Last updated:
28 August 2026 — See all updates

  1. Changes for the 2026 to 2027 exercise
  2. Trade creditors' data specifications
  3. Personal budgets data specification
  4. Pensions data specification
  5. Payroll data specification
  6. Licences data specification
  7. Housing data specifications
  8. Electoral Register data specification
  9. Council Tax data specification
  10. Transport passes and permits data specification
  11. Private supported care home residents' data specification
  12. Council Tax Reduction Scheme data specification
  13. Business Rates data specifications

Please note that data should:

  • be extracted according to the National Fraud Initiative (NFI) timetables
  • only be submitted through the secure NFI web application
  • be password-protected once extracted from the relevant systems
  • unless otherwise stated, do not include minors’ data.

Before submitting data, you must read the guidance on uploading data and the pre-upload checks you should carry out to ensure you are providing the best possible data.

The upload process automatically maps the fields in the file you are uploading by field name recognition. However, if there is no header row containing field names within the extracted data, the person uploading data will be required to manually map each field to the appropriate field on the data file upload screen. Therefore, it’s advisable to include field names in the header row within the data extract, if possible.

To find out who should supply data, refer to the data requirements guide.

Data specifications detailing the exact data we process for National Fraud Initiative pilots can be found at National Fraud Initiative: Pilot Data Specification

Read more about uploading data to the NFI.

Changes for the 2026 to 2027 exercise

The NFI reviews data specifications before each exercise. Although changes have been kept to a minimum, some are necessary to improve the matching process and the quality of matches.

Electoral Register data specification

Electoral Register data should be submitted annually for the NFI mandatory single-person discount (SPD) fraud matching. Refer to the council tax single person discount timetable.

The data should:

  • be the ‘full version’ of the Electoral Register (not the commercially available ‘edited version’)
  • relate to the appropriate registration exercise
  • include the Unique Property Reference Number (UPRN) field in your submission if it is fully or partially populated
  • be extracted and submitted after the Register is formally published

Council Tax data specification

Council Tax (CT) data should be submitted annually for the NFI mandatory single-person discount (SPD) fraud matching. Once both CT and ER data are uploaded, the NFI can generate your SPD matches (unless you encounter data issues that we need to resolve). You will not need to wait for all councils to submit their data.

View the NFI council tax single person discount timetable. Please note that you are required to password-protect each dataset once extracted from the relevant systems.

To find out who should supply council tax data, view the data requirements.

The data should:

  • include a date of birth if it is captured on your system, but we accept that this is not routinely stored. 
  • include surname and forename fields even if they are not fully populated, as they must be mapped for the upload to be accepted. If your CT system also includes an aggregated field that holds all name details, this data should also be provided so it can be mapped to the ‘Full name’ field.
  • include the Unique Property Reference Number (UPRN) field in your submission if it is populated or partially populated
  • only be current/live accounts
  • relate to all CT accounts, whether or not there is a discount or exemption (i.e., it should cover every domestic property where CT applies)

Council Tax: data specification 2026 to 2027

Transport passes and permits data specification

The Blue Badge Digital Service (BBDS) will upload data on behalf of the local authorities that have opted for this service. Please check whether you have opted in with your Blue Badge teams. If you do not use the BBDS service, then you will need to extract and upload the data locally.

Please upload data in 3 separate files:

  • current holders of a resident’s parking permit
  • current holders of a blue badge (including local schemes)
  • current holders of a concessionary travel pass (e.g., a Freedom pass)
